subject: MAP & close trajectory: MSA/DPA sequencing + order form gating for VitalCare
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & close trajectory: MSA/DPA sequencing + order form gating for VitalCare

Melissa — attaching a concise MAP and a proposed close trajectory that aligns legal review with procurement gating. High level:

- Week 1 (May 10–16): Legal receives Redwood MSA + DPA redlines; Procurement confirms order form line items and PO cadence.
- Week 2 (May 17–23): Legal turnaround on MSA/DPA (target: 3 business days for first pass); Redwood provides final pricing table for order form.
- Week 3 (May 24–30): Mutual review of final order form; sign-off and DocuSign routing.

Key dependencies we surfaced: if VitalCare requires custom data retention language in the DPA, that adds another legal pass and shifts the order form signature by ~5–7 business days. If procurement can accept the standard DPA with a short supplement, we can close on the week of May 24.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_vitalcare_20260510.xlsx (MAP with owners/milestones), VC_SOW_v1.2.pdf (baseline SOW), Redwood-Standard-MSA-2026-redlines.docx (starting redline).

Would you be able to confirm procurement windows and target PO submission date? I can sync Karthik and Marissa to walk legal through the redlines if helpful.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

From: Melissa Ortiz <m.ortiz@vitalcarehealth.com>

Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@vitalcarehealth.com>, procurement@vitalcarehealth.com
Date: 2026-05-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & close trajectory: MSA/DPA sequencing + order form gating for VitalCare

Jordan — thanks for the MAP and clear milestones. Quick answers:

- Procurement window: we have a monthly PO cycle that closes on the 25th for the next-month budget. To get a June 1 start, we need a signed order form + PO line by May 25.
- Legal: our counsel will need to run an external review on any non-standard DPA language; internal compliance (privacy) will also weight in. Typical legal roundtrip is 5–7 business days for minimal redlines, longer if there are substantive DPA changes.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood commit to a 48–72 hour turnaround on any requested clarifications once legal raises items?
2) Can you provide a single consolidated order form PDF (fillable) with the exact SKU/pricing to hand to procurement?

We reviewed VC_SOW_v1.2 and have a few scope clarifications — I’ll add inline comments and share back by EOD.

—Melissa
Melissa Ortiz
Director, Procurement | VitalCare Health
m.ortiz@vitalcarehealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Melissa Ortiz <m.ortiz@vitalcarehealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & close trajectory: MSA/DPA sequencing + order form gating for VitalCare

Melissa — quick operational clarifications from Legal/Ops so we can align the MAP: 

1) Turnaround: we can commit to a 48–72 hour response SLA for clarification questions and non-substantive redline acceptance during the active close window. For DPA substantive language (data residency, deletion timelines outside our standard), we will need product and privacy sign-off which may take up to 4 business days.

2) Order form: attaching a single consolidated order form PDF for procurement that includes: SKUs, unit pricing, billing cadence, and the standard payment terms. If procurement needs Net 45 instead of Net 30 we can escalate approval — that will affect finance sign-off and could add 2–3 business days.

3) Preferred sequencing (recommended):
- Day 0: Shared MAP + attach MSA/DPA redlines + consolidated order form (we’ve done this).
- Legal review window (VitalCare): 3–7 business days depending on DPA changes. During this window, procurement prepares PO draft in parallel.
- Legal sign-off -> Procurement issues PO -> DocuSign routing.

If procurement must wait for an executed DPA before issuing the PO (versus signing the order form contingent on execution), we’ll need to flag resource allocation dates in the MAP (so teams know tentative start dates).

Attaching: Redwood_OrderForm_VC_20260511.pdf (consolidated order form).

Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

From: Melissa Ortiz <m.ortiz@vitalcarehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@vitalcarehealth.com>, procurement@vitalcarehealth.com
Date: 2026-05-11T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & close trajectory: MSA/DPA sequencing + order form gating for VitalCare

Thanks Karthik — that sequencing makes sense. A couple of clarifications from procurement/legal intake after reviewing your materials:

- We raised three DPA items that are likely "substantive": data deletion timeline for backups, subprocessor notification cadence, and a narrow amendment to incident notification SLAs for PHI-containing events. Those will likely move us into the 7–10 business day bin unless Redwood can accept a limited supplement instead of rewriting core DPA sections.
- Procurement confirmed they can prepare a PO draft in parallel but will not issue payment until the DPA is fully accepted (legal policy). That means signature sequencing is: MSA + DPA execution -> order form -> PO.

Action items we need from Redwood:
1) Proposal for a DPA supplement that addresses the three points above (Melissa to review). Can your privacy team draft a short supplement this week?
2) Confirmation on Net 30 vs Net 45 (procurement prefers Net 45).

I’ll circulate our counsel’s redline on the MSA by EOB tomorrow. If we can get a DPA supplement draft by May 14, we should still be in range for a May 25 PO if legal reviews run quickly.

—Melissa

Melissa — appreciate the level-setting and the three DPA focus points. Quick commitments from Redwood: 

- We will produce a DPA supplement draft addressing backup deletion windows, subprocessor notifications, and incident SLA narrow-tailoring by end of day May 14. That supplement will be additive (supplement + standard DPA) to minimize legal churn.
- Finance: Redwood can accept Net 45 for VitalCare; finance will issue confirmation within 24 hours. That should remove the Net terms blocker.
- Response SLA: we confirm 48–72 hour response time for clarification/redline resolution during the active close window.

Next steps I will execute this afternoon: publish an updated MAP that includes the "supplement" task owner (Privacy: Karthik) and a sticky milestone that marks "PO submission by May 25 contingent on DPA supplement acceptance." I’ll share the updated MAP link and the DocuSign order form preview to procurement.

If that all sounds good I’ll schedule a 30-minute alignment call for Thursday (May 14) — proposed attendees: Melissa, Sanjay, Jordan, Karthik, and one procurement rep.

Thanks — Jordan
